definition: Amplitude spectrum is an image property that describes how much energy or contrast is present at different spatial frequencies or orientations. In this context, changes in the amplitude spectrum away from the regular pattern typical of natural scenes were linked to greater visual unpleasantness or discomfort.

reasons: The packet does not provide a direct definition of “amplitude spectrum” as an image property describing “how much energy or contrast” at “spatial frequencies or orientations”; it only discusses that the amplitude spectrum (and related spatial-frequency/orientation spectra) can deviate from natural-scene regularities and affect unpleasantness ratings.

The claim that “changes in the amplitude spectrum away from the regular pattern typical of natural scenes were linked to greater visual unpleasantness or discomfort” is supported in the packet, but the definition also contains an unsupported general characterization (energy/contrast at spatial frequencies or orientations).

The packet supports amplitude spectrum as a spatial-frequency property, but not the claim that it describes energy or contrast at different orientations; orientation is treated separately in the source as an orientation spectrum.
